facts.text: Pocopson Township was incorporated on September 13, 1849, carved from Pennsbury, Thornbury, and Upper Oxford townships, and named after a Lenape term meaning “smoky place” along Pocopson Creek.
A covered bridge built in 1857 and the 1870 Wilmington and Northern Railroad spurred businesses at Pocopson Station, turning it into a local hub.
The Pocopson Township Historical Committee actively preserves local sites, including the Wilkinson House and Lenape Bridge, guiding planning to maintain the area’s historic character.
